newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul renews stock repurchase plan.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul renews stock repurchase plan.

text.p: St. Paul Cos said Friday its board renewed authority to repurchase common stock of the company in 1997 and also took actions to facilitate increased stock ownership by certain key executives.

Under the plan, management has authority to buy back up to five percent of St. Paul's common stock over the next 12 months. It has repurchased stock in each of the past three years under similar authority, including 1.4 million shares in 1996, 768,000 in 1995 and 860,000 in 1994.

St. Paul's board said it made special one-time option grants to certain executives in December. The earliest date on which any of those options will become exercisable is December 2000, and they will expire in December 2001.

Half of the options granted to each executive would become exercisable only if the 20-day average stock price reached $100 per share. The other half would become exercisable if the 20-day average price hit $110 per share.

In addition, the board will recommend shareholder approval of a leveraged stock purchase program for the same group of executives who receive the special option grants. This program complements those option awards and provides for loans from the company in order for the executives to acquire the shares.
St. Paul is a group of companies providing property-liability insurance products and services.
